item: The write gate measures a long hold's split after the gate is free, so an interrupt in the measuring cannot keep the gate
refs: independent read of PR #1429's head, finding L1 (and nits N1, N2, N3); coordinator 17 Oct yes to C1, C3 to C5; PR #1435; independent read of PR #1435's head, finding M1
summary: release() computed the per-bucket breakdown of a hold of HOLD_RECORD_S (30 s) or more while the releasing thread still owned the gate with its depth already at 0, above the line that frees it, so a KeyboardInterrupt or a MemoryError inside that loop over the ledger left the owner set for good: a second release returns at the depth check and every other acquire queues (the reader's probe: another thread's acquire(timeout=0.5) returned False with the owner still set; the real route is a script's write_lock -> release on the main thread, R163). It is now computed after the gate is free and the next waiter woken, still under the gate's lock (the woken head cannot reset the ledger before it takes the lock), with the hold's start passed in because _held_since is cleared by then. Tests: the release raises the signal and the next writer is granted, for KeyboardInterrupt and MemoryError (both red without the change), and a raw connection's commit still open at the release is counted in the exact split (red when the start is not passed). Same push, words only: the registry, the dependency doc and the phase-table row count seven SQLAlchemy functions, not six (N1); the storage guard's comment no longer calls execute and commit the only moments a checkout pins the log (N2); a tautological assert of a sum of three typed constants is deleted from the slot test and its figures kept in the comment (N3). Not folded here: the paused card-audit bundle member recorded as an error (L2) goes to the diagnostics-bundle follow-on, the exclusive-window one-instruction hole (N4) to the shutdown-WAL bundle after #1431, the second loop back-edge in storage_events.end (N5) is an open item. The independent read of #1435's head (M1) found the rest of the measuring still above the free, and on EVERY outermost release: the clock, the totals, the peak holder's name and the per-holder row. All of it now follows the free and the wake-up, the breakdown last so a failure in its loops does not drop the figures before it; the interrupt test is parametrized over the per-holder row, and a pin on the source of release() requires that no call runs between the last read of the branch and the free (red on the old order).
